verdict_reason: Both estimators reproduce Kornblith's released code. Fetched google-research/representation_similarity/Demo.ipynb this pass and ran it head-to-head: on 40 random (n, d) cases BLME's _linear_cka matches feature_space_linear_cka(debiased=False) to worst relative 4.10e-07 (float32 input rounding) and _linear_cka_debiased matches feature_space_linear_cka(debiased=True) to 4.45e-08; on the notebook's own seeded demo (seed 1337, X = randn(100,10), Y = randn(100,10)+X) the reference gives 0.55761326 / 0.51345649 and BLME 0.55761328 / 0.51345649. The two objections from my last pass are both resolved in substance: undefined cases now return NaN rather than a false 0.0 (with a scale-free relative degeneracy test, so CKA(aX, bY) = CKA(X, Y) survives), and the debiased family is now labelled as removing the d/N NULL FLOOR rather than as a comparability fix -- a label I verified in both directions (floor 0.0216 -> 0.2630 biased over d = 512..8192 at the study N = 23,272 against |debiased| <= 1.5e-4; and Pearson 0.99999980 between the biased and debiased layer-pair matrices on real gpt2 activations). BLME's new feature-space HSIC is algebraically identical to its own Gram-space form (worst relative 1.45e-15, and 0.0e+00 on the reduced form). The defects that remain are runtime and NaN-policy, not fidelity.
comparable_reason: Measured on the 66-model zoo (results/blme_verified_a, d_model 512-7168, n_layers 6-64), not on a small sample. Only ONE of the eight biased summaries is size-linked: avg_adjacent_cka rho(d_model) = +0.546, rho(n_layers) = +0.588, rho(params) = +0.525. The study's headline predictors are clean -- min_offdiag_cka +0.084 / -0.005 / +0.070 and max_offdiag_cka +0.057 / -0.024 / +0.004 -- with std_offdiag_cka (-0.284 / -0.329 / -0.339) and early_late_cka (-0.316 / -0.099 / -0.279) in between. This is a clear UPGRADE from the rho = +0.946 figure the code comment quotes, which came from 8 models. What keeps it off GREEN is a real, measured architectural offset in the biased estimator: at the study's N = 23,272 two INDEPENDENT Gaussian clouds score 0.0216 / 0.0318 / 0.0809 / 0.1501 / 0.2630 at d = 512 / 768 / 2048 / 4096 / 8192, so a wide model's CKA cannot go below a floor a quarter of the way up the scale, while the debiased twin reads |value| <= 1.5e-4 at every width.
github_reason: Fetched Demo.ipynb from google-research/google-research master and executed its gram_linear / center_gram / cka / _debiased_dot_product_similarity_helper / feature_space_linear_cka verbatim against BLME. Biased: worst relative 4.097e-07 over 40 random (n in 30..200, d in 3..40) centered/scaled/offset pairs. Debiased: worst relative 4.453e-08. Notebook demo cell (seed 1337): reference 0.55761326 biased / 0.51345649 debiased, BLME 0.55761328 / 0.51345649. Separately checked BLME's own two debiased routes against each other -- _debiased_hsic_features vs _debiased_hsic on explicit Gram matrices -- worst relative 1.447e-15.
paper_reason: Kornblith et al. 2019 (arXiv:1905.00414) publishes CKA as heatmaps over CIFAR-10 CNN layers (Fig. 2, Fig. 5-8) and reports no scalar a text-model harness could reproduce; the reproducible anchor is the released notebook's own demo output, which BLME matches to 4.06e-08 (biased) and 7.19e-09 (debiased). Component-level anchors also hold: the paper's stated d/N bias of the biased estimator is reproduced exactly -- two independent Gaussians at n=256 score 0.0300 / 0.1114 / 0.3354 / 0.6668 at d = 8 / 32 / 128 / 512 against -0.0002 / +0.0002 / +0.0032 / +0.0005 debiased, matching the values quoted in the code comment to within 0.003. PARTIAL because the paper itself publishes no reproducible scalar.
confounds_reason: Mechanism confirmed but effect small in the shipped columns. The biased estimator carries a width-dependent null floor rising from 0.0216 (d=512) to 0.2630 (d=8192) at the study N -- a genuine d_model artifact of up to a quarter of the [0,1] scale. At n=66 real models, however, only avg_adjacent_cka tracks size (rho(d_model) +0.546, rho(n_layers) +0.588); mean_offdiag (+0.064 / -0.045), min_offdiag (+0.084 / -0.005), max_offdiag (+0.057 / -0.024) and first_middle (+0.090 / +0.018) are all essentially flat. On real gpt2 activations the biased and debiased matrices agree to Pearson 0.99999980 (max |difference| 7.56e-04), so the floor is not what real layer pairs are sitting on -- but it would be for a genuinely unrelated pair in a wide model, which is exactly the case the debiased family exists to cover.
defects: STILL BLOCKING, AND MEASURED THIS PASS: the debiased family does not fit inside the study's own 3,600 s task_timeout (run_blme.py:198) for large models, even after the feature-space rewrite. At N = 23,272 and 64 threads: biased pair 0.196 s, debiased pair 6.549 s at d = 5120 -- a 33x ratio -- giving 0.96 h for a 32-layer model, 1.97 h at 46 layers, 3.78 h at 64 and 5.89 h at 80. The rewrite is a genuine ~10x improvement over the Gram route (which extrapolates to 50-80 s per pair, i.e. 34.7 h at L=64, and 24.9 GB against the feature route's measured 6.64 GB peak RSS), but the task still cannot complete for the widest, deepest models in the zoo.

DEAD CODE DOING THE MOST EXPENSIVE OPERATION IN THE FUNCTION, TWICE. _debiased_hsic_features computes `xtx_sq = float((X.t() @ X).pow(2).sum())` and `yty_sq = float((Y.t() @ Y).pow(2).sum())` -- two O(N*D^2) GEMMs -- and then discards them at `_ = (xtx_sq, yty_sq)`. Neither value reaches the return statement. Measured cost of the dead lines alone at N = 23,272: 1.80x at d=768 (0.190 s -> 0.106 s), 1.92x at d=2048, 2.64x at d=5120 (3.910 s -> 1.479 s), with the reduced form agreeing to relative 0.0e+00. Deleting two lines takes a 64-layer model from 3.78 h to roughly 1.4 h.

The per-pair normalizer redundancy I flagged last pass is NOT moot after the feature-space switch, contrary to the note in the fix. _linear_cka_debiased still calls _debiased_hsic_features(X, X) and (Y, Y) inside the pair loop although each depends on ONE layer only, so hxx and hyy are recomputed L times each. Hoisting them out of the loop is a further ~3x on top of the dead-code fix.

THE DEBIASED FAMILY IS A NEAR-EXACT DUPLICATE OF THE BIASED FAMILY ON REAL DATA. Measured on gpt2 at the study N = 23,272 over all 66 layer pairs: Pearson r = 0.99999980, max |biased - debiased| = 7.56e-04, mean 0.7681 vs 0.7679; the four summaries read 0.8687/0.8685, 0.7545/0.7540, 0.0344/0.0341, 0.0428/0.0419. So the study pays a 33x runtime penalty for four columns that carry essentially no information the existing four lack. They earn their place only for wide models where a genuinely unrelated layer pair would otherwise be floored at 0.26 -- which no stored run can yet demonstrate, since the columns are new. Prefix them `_meta_` (they are a diagnostic, not features) or gate them on d/N.

CODE: the NaN policy is still asymmetric between the two families, unchanged from my last pass. mean/std/min/max_offdiag_cka and min/max/std_adjacent_cka use np.mean / np.min / np.std, which PROPAGATE a NaN, while debiased_* use np.nanmean / np.nanmin, which DROP it. One degenerate layer therefore blanks four biased summaries while the debiased ones silently report a value computed on the surviving pairs.

CODE: avg_adjacent_cka still falls back to 0.0 via _stat(diagonal_off1, np.mean, 0.0) while every sibling falls back to NaN -- the exact false-zero the NaN fix was written to eliminate, left in the one place a 1-layer model would hit it.

THE DOUBLE-CENTERING COMMENT IS STILL UNREPRODUCIBLE, AND I NOW HAVE THE COUNTER-MEASUREMENT. It claims dropping the second centering pass 'moved CKA from 0.7787 to 0.3069 against a float64 truth of 0.7787'. Measured over mean in {0, 1e2, 1e4, 1e6} x sd in {1e-3, 1} in float32: single vs double centering differ by at most 7.05e-04, and at the very case the comment describes (mean 1e4, sd 1e-3) single gives 0.580539 and double 0.580559 against a float64 truth of 0.708522 -- the second pass moves 2.0e-05 where the error is 0.128. The second centering is harmless but it is not the correction the comment says it is.
